complexity.notes: Re-sorting the entire list every round makes this O(n^2 log n); a ||binary max-heap (e.g. heapq with negated weights)|| would bring it down to O(n log n). `stones.pop() and stones.pop()` is a needlessly cute idiom — it relies on the popped value being truthy to execute the second pop, so it would silently skip a pop if a weight were ever 0 (impossible under the stated positive-weight precondition, but two plain statements are clearer). Using `stones.sort()` in place would also avoid building a new list each round.
complexity.summary: Simulates the process directly: each round it re-sorts the whole list, pops the two heaviest stones, and pushes back the difference when they differ, until at most one stone remains.
